ground_truth.mechanism: `_num` calls `math.isfinite` on any Python int before range-checking it, so a huge JSON integer (for example `dpr` = 10**400) raises OverflowError rather than ProbeRefused; the route catches only ProbeRefused, so the error escapes to the daemon's generic handler, which answers 409 'request failed (OverflowError)' and logs a stack trace instead of the fixed 400 refusal (the reviewer's '500' is wrong, but the escape is real).

non_issues.claim: The mock server copies the conflict check instead of calling the real route handler, so removing the check from the real route goes unnoticed by the face tests.
non_issues.why_not: The face-suite mock (tests/face/hud_v2_mock_browser.py) is a hand-written stand-in for the HTTP routes by design. It reimplements every route, including the profile, tab and approval-card 409s. Its job is to test the HUD against that contract, not to test the daemon's route code. The real gate at jarvis/v2/browser/routes.py:216-218 is covered directly: tests/v2/direct_capture_check.py:160-171 sends PATCH /browser/settings with direct_capture true and expects 409 before a pass and success after one. Removing the real check would fail that test, so the regression the claim describes would still be caught. The finding's own scenario admits this coverage.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p2, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: When no crop is applied, the probe's sampled values come from real tab content and are saved to disk, which contradicts the module's stated guarantee.
non_issues.why_not: The code never samples a frame that was not cropped. grabCroppedFrame throws DirectRefused('not_cropped') when cropTo is missing (line 188) or rejects (line 191), and only reaches grabFrame after `await cropTo` has resolved and set crop.applied = true. In that case runProbe catches the refusal and returns with samples still [] (directProbe.ts:66-86). So when the crop is not applied, no tab pixels are read or written to the report, and the docstring's guarantee holds.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p3, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: The capture path only checks the persisted switch and never checks that a probe passed on the current daemon, so after a restart or a hand edit, captures go through without any probe.
non_issues.why_not: The plan says this is intended. The probe pass only gates turning the switch on through the PATCH route (routes.py:216). After a restart the switch keeps its saved value. So capture_direct is meant to check only the persisted switch (captures.py:242) and not look for a pass from the current daemon. A hand edit of browser.json is the owner's own action on owner-only state, so it does not bypass the agent boundary.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p4, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: A second HUD window keeps an outdated copy of the setting for up to the refresh interval and still starts the screen-share grab after the owner disabled it elsewhere.
non_issues.why_not: The plan expects a HUD window to sometimes hold an old copy of the switch and makes the daemon the guard: it refuses a Direct capture reference while the switch is off. That is the 409 the finding itself describes. The capture also needs the owner's own trusted press and the owner accepting Chrome's share prompt. The pixels stay in that HUD window and are thrown away when the daemon refuses, so nothing reaches an agent. The stale window is the intended, documented design, not a defect.

non_issues.claim: The direct capture handler checks only the current input-hold flag and never compares the hold epoch from before and after, so an approval card that came and went during the capture is missed.
non_issues.why_not: The daemon never sees the Direct pixels. The HUD grabs the frame before it sends the POST, and the plan gives the HUD the job of handling an approval card that appears during the capture: it checks for blocked before the share prompt, stops the tracks if a card appears during any await, and re-checks coverage at the grab. capture_direct is a short synchronous handler, so an epoch read at its start would come after the HUD's grab had already finished. Copying capture_page's capture_hold_epoch guard could therefore not catch a card that came and went during the grab, which is the scenario the claim describes. In capture_page the epoch matters because the daemon itself takes the capture inside host.capture_look; Direct has no daemon-side capture for a card to overlap. What the daemon does check (switch, mode, binding, and input_held before and after minting) covers the short window it actually spans.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p10, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: The code finds the allowed overlay by its position next to the frame in the DOM, so reordering the elements would make every capture be refused as covered.
non_issues.why_not: This describes a hypothetical future refactor, not a defect in the current code. FrameHost appends the frame and then the shield as siblings, so `frame.nextElementSibling` is always the `.frameshield` and captures work today. If the order were ever reversed, the guard would refuse captures as 'covered' rather than let a covered frame through, which is a fail-closed outcome and not a bug in this change.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p14, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: The daemon reference is requested before the gesture is checked for staleness, which can leave orphaned capture rows, and the later error path never offers the Remote fallback.
non_issues.why_not: The finding's scenario does not happen. captureDirect checks live(), which includes valid(token), straight after encoding (directCapture.ts:253-254). A gesture that goes stale during encode therefore throws DirectRefused('stale') before api.directCapture is ever called, and no row is created. The only window left is the daemon request itself. The Remote path (BrowserCapture.tsx:106) has the same window and handles it the same way, with the re-check at :107. Any row left behind that way is harmless: the store expires rows after 24 hours and caps both entry count and bytes (captures.py:23, :70-73, :108-113). The other half of the claim is about the catch at :113. It handles generic errors, such as a failed daemon reference request. Those are not Direct refusals, and opening the page in Remote would not fix them. The Remote offer is deliberately tied to DirectRefused reasons at :101, so leaving it out at :113 is not a defect.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p15, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-22

non_issues.claim: The Direct capture handler adds the URL-only row before its final owner/input-hold re-check, so a refusal at that point returns 409 and leaves a stored row whose id never reaches the HUD.
non_issues.why_not: The re-check after the add is real, but the leftover row does no harm. Its id is a random 128-bit token that is never returned, and owner resolution needs that exact id, so nothing can reach the row. Its contents are only the URL that the same guard has already checked. The store keeps at most 16 rows and drops each after 24 h, so the row just ages out. At worst it takes one slot for that time. The Remote capture path that existed before this change does the same thing on purpose: it adds the row, then checks `owner_current`/held again. The Direct handler copies that pattern rather than adding a new defect.
non_issues.citation: jarvis/v2/browser/captures.py:110-121 (bounded store, random id), jarvis/v2/browser/captures.py:211-215 (same add-then-recheck in capture_page), jarvis/v2/browser/captures.py:255-263
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p17, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23

non_issues.claim: Work done between the press and getDisplayMedia can use up Chrome's transient user activation, and the NotAllowedError that follows is mapped to 'cancelled', so the owner is told they cancelled a prompt they never saw.
non_issues.why_not: The claim does not hold up in the code. The work done before the prompt is bounded: `beforeCapture` → `uncover` waits at most 3 s (`deadline=Date.now()+3000`, and it throws once that passes), then two animation frames and `CropTarget.fromElement` follow, which take milliseconds. That stays inside Chrome's roughly 5 s transient-activation window. Also, the Screen Capture spec says a missing transient activation rejects `getDisplayMedia` with `InvalidStateError`, not `NotAllowedError`, and Chrome follows that ('getDisplayMedia requires transient activation from a user gesture'). Line 170 sends `InvalidStateError` to prompt 'error' / reason 'failed', not 'cancelled'. So an expired gesture would never show the 'share prompt was cancelled' message. Only a real denial or dismissal (`NotAllowedError`/`AbortError`) is reported as cancelled, which is the intended mapping.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p18, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23

non_issues.claim: The settings PATCH reads a passing probe result and enables the switch in separate steps, so a failed probe recorded in between leaves Direct capture enabled despite the latest failure.
non_issues.why_not: The design only makes a passing probe a condition for turning the switch on. It never says a later failed probe turns the switch off. The plan states that the switch keeps its saved value even after a restart, when no passing probe exists. The capture route (captures.py:242) checks only the setting and never the probe. So a failed probe recorded just after the PATCH, with no race involved, also leaves Direct capture on, and that is intended. The race the claim describes leads to the same end state as a failed probe that arrives a moment later. Both requests are also the owner's own, on owner-only routes.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p21, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23

non_issues.claim: The coverage sampling grid is inset by the 8 px edge margin, so an opaque element with no listed overlay role or class over the iframe's outer band is never detected and ends up in the captured picture.
non_issues.why_not: The 8 px inset is a documented design choice. The browser notes say the 5×5 hit-test grid is "inset 8 px past the panes' transparent resize handles", and the code comment at directCapture.ts:84-85 says the same. By design, the coverage check is a sparse 25-point sample plus a list of known overlay roles and selectors. It was never meant to test every pixel. An unlisted element sitting between any two grid points escapes it just as easily as one in the edge band, so the band is not a separate defect. The plan (step 2) specifies exactly this check, a 5×5 grid plus role/known-selector overlays, and the code implements it as written.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p23, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23
